label: Radiation dose on the Mars surface from galactic cosmic rays (Curiosity RAD, Gale 2012–13)
source: Hassler et al. 2014, Science (Curiosity RAD at Gale crater, absorbed 0.21 mGy/day); SwRI release: https://www.swri.org/press-release/swri-scientists-publish-first-radiation-measurements-surface-mars
note: Measured at Gale crater. Varies with the solar cycle (~0.44–0.74 mSv/day); Jezero assumed similar.

label: Radiation dose during the cruise to Mars
source: Zeitlin et al. 2013, Science — RAD inside MSL during cruise
note: Measured behind MSL's own shielding.

label: Earth-to-Mars transit time
source: SwRI / Zeitlin et al. release (180-day trip): https://www.swri.org/press-release/swri-scientists-publish-first-radiation-measurements-surface-mars
note: Used only to estimate dose already received on arrival.

label: NASA career radiation limit (NASA effective dose)
source: NASA OCHMO Radiation Protection technical brief / NASA-STD-3001

unit: mSv (NASA effective dose, per design-reference solar particle event)
label: NASA limit for a solar particle event
source: NASA-STD-3001 Vol 1 Rev B [V1 4031], via the NASA OCHMO radiation technical brief
note: The older 30-day blood-forming-organ limit (250 mGy-Eq) is superseded by the effective-dose limit per design-reference solar particle event.

label: Radiation dose an astronaut at Gale would have received in the May 2024 solar storm (as reported by NASA/JPL)
note: JPL compares it to ~30 chest X-rays and says it would not have been deadly; the particles reached Mars in tens of minutes. RAD team material indicates the figure may be the event's peak daily rate rather than a total (event total possibly ~1.7 mGy). The app uses JPL's figure as reported.

label: Dose reduction from standing next to a butte
source: Ehresmann et al. 2021, Natural Radiation Shielding on Mars Measured With the MSL/RAD Instrument, JGR Planets 126(8), e2021JE006851
note: About 4–5% near one butte at Gale (19% of sky blocked), Butte M12, sols 1456–1467. One butte at Gale, not a general rule.

label: Balance/coordination problems after long spaceflight (about 1–2 weeks)
source: NASA Functional Task Test / Pilot Field Test (Miller et al. 2018, Aerosp Med Hum Perform 89(9):805): recovery ~6–16 days after long flights
note: 7 is a central value of the ~6–16 day range.

label: Walking speed on landing day vs normal
source: Team estimate based on post-flight sensorimotor findings
note: Ramps linearly to 1.0 by sensorimotor_recovery_days.

label: Bone loss in weightlessness (1–1.5%/month)
note: Midpoint of 1–1.5% per month.

label: Far-sighted vision shift from spaceflight (SANS), +0.5 to +1.75 D
Landmark recognition range with vision changes
note: Illustrative assumption: no study measures landmark range; SANS mainly blurs near vision.

label: Design EVA duration
note: Plus ~2 h pre/post. For comparison, the ISS EMU supports ~7 h.

label: Consumables reserve kept back
source: Moore & Marmolejo 2014, Extravehicular Activity (EVA) Hardware & Operations Overview (NTRS 20140009556): EMU supports a 7 h EVA = 15 min egress + 6 h useful work + 15 min ingress + 30 min reserve
note: Shuttle/ISS EMU number, used here for a Mars suit.

label: Average metabolic rate during EVA
note: Shown as context; not used in maths v1. Apollo walk-back planning used 1440 BTU/h.

label: Suited walk-back speed
source: Apollo Lunar Surface Journal, Apollo 11 gaits (walk-back planning values)
note: Lunar number used for Mars (0.38 g) — estimate. ALSJ gives ~3.6 km/h for ~1 h walk-backs and ~2.7 km/h for longer ones.

label: Safety margin on walk-home time (+20%)
source: Team estimate, inspired by the Apollo walk-back constraint (stay within walking distance of the lander on remaining suit consumables)
note: Apollo planned walk-backs with a high metabolic rate (1440 vs ~1024 BTU/h, ~+40%) rather than a time pad; 1.2 is the team's simpler equivalent. Treat as an estimate.

label: Max slope allowed before sol 7
Max slope allowed after recovery
Suit cooling (water membrane evaporator, SWME) works only below ~7 Torr ambient pressure
source: NASA Mars PLSS status and plan, ICES-2026-126 (NTRS 20260003024)
note: A true sublimator cannot work above water's triple point (~611 Pa) and Jezero is ~718 Pa, so a Mars suit uses an SWME, tested to ~10 Torr. Key name kept for compatibility.

label: Typical surface pressure at Jezero (~5.4 Torr)
note: Varies ~±10–15% with season and 10–35 Pa through the day.

label: Mean air temperature at Jezero
note: Day–night swing ~50–60 °C.

label: Cold warning threshold
Be heading home by (cooling before dusk)
Dust-devil warning window start
source: Newman et al. 2022 — Perseverance saw >4 dust devils per sol, peak 12–13 LTST
note: Window widened by 1 h each side.

label: Dust-devil warning window end
Peak dust-devil wind seen at Jezero
note: Largest seen ~270 m wide, pressure drop up to ~6.5 Pa.

label: What a 32 m/s Mars wind pushes like on Earth (same dynamic pressure)
source: Team calculation: same dynamic pressure, Mars surface air ~70x thinner than Earth (rho ~0.017 kg/m3 at 718 Pa and ~218 K vs 1.225 kg/m3)
note: 32 × sqrt(ρMars/ρEarth) ≈ 3.8 m/s. Force equivalence only: the wind pushes like a ~3.8 m/s breeze on Earth, but it still carries dust.

label: Normal dust optical depth at Jezero
note: ~0.3–0.5 outside storms.

label: Dust optical depth in the Jan 2022 Jezero storm
note: τ rose from ~0.3 to ~1.7–2; wind sensors damaged.

label: Dust caution threshold
Dust return threshold
Dust layer depth used to turn τ into visibility
note: Near-surface dust scale height is ~8–11 km and the CO₂ scale height ~10.8 km. Example: τ 2 → ~22 km; τ 10 → ~4 km. Horizontal visibility is indicative only; terrain limits the view first.

label: Perchlorate in Martian soil (0.5–1%)
source: Univ. of Colorado, Mar 2025 — Martian dust health risks
note: Thyroid risk → dust-off before entry.

label: How much longer a sol is than an Earth day
source: Sol = 24 h 39 min 35 s; circadian study (PMC1934931)

label: One Mars hour (1/24 sol) in Earth minutes
Astronaut eye height in suit
Position uncertainty growth without a fix (dead reckoning)
source: Team estimate (pedestrian dead reckoning drifts ~2–5% of distance)
note: Uncertainty circle = last fix uncertainty + 3% of distance walked since; reset by Skyline Fix. Heading from gyro/sun sensor (Mars has no global magnetic field, so no compass).

label: How fast a dust devil drifts across the ground
source: Team estimate: dust devils travel with the background wind, typically a few m/s
note: Only used for the illustrative map animation.
